*You weren't sure what you were expecting when you followed that map to the abandoned church, but it definitely wasn't this. The church, decrepit and overgrown from the outside, seemed to pulse with something almost alive as you neared it. The mirrors inside shouldn't have been that reflective, smudged with age and grime, and yet they shone with a strange, unnatural clarity. The head priest's promises of sacrifice sounded half insane and half... too real. The cult, if that’s even what it was, wasn’t just about worship—it was about giving up everything. Your body, your mind, your soul to something far beyond the understanding of mere mortals.*

*And just as you were about to bolt, well… you saw what the mirrors showed to those who ‘opted out’. And as you tried reasoning with the priest you were held by the hem of your robe. The burly man had been pretty damn convincing with his threats, his body swelling like some sort of unholy balloon until you could practically see his muscles bulging through his robes. That wasn't somebody you wanted to mess with. At that moment you could see his bald globe is peppered with black and white eyes, all looking down at you. Obviously you agreed to join out of peer pressure.*

*Stepping through that mirror felt like tearing the fragile membrane of reality itself. The air thickened, becoming a soup of whispers and shadows that clawed at your thoughts. The drone-like figures you passed barely registered as human anymore, their vacant eyes and shuffling steps more like walking corpses than anything with agency or life. And then there was that priest droning on about how they were all going to be sacrificed—to him. And the ‘Master’, standing just beyond those huge double doors that loomed before you like the maw of some carnivorous beast ready to swallow you whole. You barely see there, but made out the head with lots of holes and pair of hovering black claws.*

*The moment you stepped into the room, those double doors slammed shut behind you with a finality that echoed in the hollow chamber of what was left of your sanity. Stepping deeper into the shadows suddenly you felt a splitting headache, ringing and hurting like nine hells. Just push through...
